# Adjudication Task — Chapter 219

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃219화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|인류는 대격변 초기부터 지금까지, 숱한 죽음과 파괴의 경험을 바탕으로 몬스터를 분류하고 서열을 정립해 왔다.
  6|
  7|그에 따라 서식하는 몬스터의 등급에 따라 해당 게이트의 등급도 정해졌다.
  8|
  9|그러나…….
 10|
 11|‘어디에나 예외는 있는 법.’
 12|
 13|변이 게이트가 바로 그랬다. 인간이 정한 테두리를 벗어난 그것은 말 그대로 변이(變異), 그 자체였다.
 14|
 15|인류에게 있어 여전히 불가사의로 취급받는 게이트라는 공간에, 또 다른 변수가 끼어든 것이다.
 16|
 17|‘최악이지.’
 18|
 19|F급 게이트에서 D급 몬스터가, D급 게이트에서 B급 몬스터가 나타날 수도 있다.
 20|
 21|그것만으로도 끔찍한 악몽인데 더 큰 문제가 하나 남아 있었다.
 22|
 23|‘레어 몬스터(Rare Monster).’
 24|
 25|생각지도 못한 상위 몬스터와 마주친 것도 지랄 같은데, 그렇게 출현한 놈들은 하나같이 동급의 몬스터를 뛰어넘는 힘을 지녔다.
 26|
 27|레어 몬스터라는 단어는 그때 처음 탄생했다.
 28|
 29|그리고 얼마 지나지 않아 한 가지 의견이 제기되었다.
 30|
 31|
 32|
 33|‘그럼 A급 변이 게이트에서 나타나는 레어 몬스터들은? 같은 급으로 치기에는 너무 강하지 않나?’
 34|
 35|
 36|
 37|헌터들에게 A급이란 한 번의 각성으로 도달할 수 있는 최고점의 영역.
 38|
 39|그중에서도 강자로 인정받은 자들에게는 랭커라는 영광스러운 칭호가 부여되었다.
 40|
 41|이는 몬스터에게도 적용되는 문제였다. 관련 학계의 수많은 갑론을박 끝에 새로운 명칭이 생겨났다.
 42|
 43|‘네임드 몬스터(Named Monster).’
 44|
 45|A급이라는 울타리를 벗어난 진정한 괴수들.
 46|
 47|홀로 살아 돌아온 1팀장은 바로 그 네임드 몬스터가 있다고 말했다.
 48|
 49|우리가 서 있는 바로 공간, 와이번의 둥지에.
 50|
 51|“개소리!”
 52|
 53|거칠게 소리친 원명훈이 1팀장의 멱살을 움켜잡았다.
 54|
 55|“네임드 몬스터라니, 그딴 게 여기 있을 리가 없어.”
 56|
 57|“저, 정말입니다. 제 눈으로 똑똑히 봤다고요.”
 58|
 59|1팀장이 떨리는 목소리로 말을 이었다.
 60|
 61|“평범한 와이번보다 몇 배는 거대했습니다. 두 눈으로 직접 보면서도 믿기지 않을 정도로.”
 62|
 63|“닥쳐!”
 64|
 65|그러나 1팀장이 네임드 몬스터에게 받은 공포는 상상 이상으로 컸다.
 66|
 67|A급 헌터라는 이름이 무색하게도, 그는 일곱 살 어린아이처럼 겁에 질려 있었다.
 68|
 69|“그놈은 지금까지 상대한 와이번과는 격이 다릅니다. 지금 당장 도망쳐야 해요.”
 70|
 71|“김종훈, 너 이 새끼…….”
 72|
 73|뿌드득.
 74|
 75|원명훈은 이를 갈았지만 그뿐이었다.
 76|
 77|비록 모든 면에서 기대 이하의 모습을 보여 주긴 했지만 그 역시 한때 랭커까지 올랐던 A급 헌터. 이미 이 자리의 모두가 알고 있는 사실을 모를 리 없었다.
 78|
 79|원명훈이 1팀장을 윽박지르는 것은 자신의 두려움을 감추려는 방어기제일 뿐이다.
 80|
 81|‘이미 변이 게이트의 조짐은 있었을 텐데.’
 82|
 83|이미 3년 전 직접 겪어 본 일이기에 잘 알고 있다.
 84|
 85|이상하리만치 적은 몬스터의 출현. 그리고 처치한 몬스터에 비해 후할 정도로 많은 마정석의 양.
 86|
 87|나는 후자에 관한 사실은 모르고 있었다. 부산물 처리는 스타 길드의 소관이고, 제아무리 협동 레이드라고 해도 모든 걸 결정하는 지휘관은 원명훈이다.
 88|
 89|‘그런데 그 지휘관이 똥을 싸 버렸네.’
 90|
 91|이건 사소한 판단 미스 수준이 아니다.
 92|
 93|저 황무지 어딘가에서 우리를 노리고 있는 놈은 평범한 와이번이 아니라 네임드 몬스터니까.
 94|
 95|“이런 씨발…….”
 96|
 97|거친 욕설을 내뱉는 원명훈에게 최 팀장이 말했다.
 98|
 99|“진정하시죠. 현 상황에서는 당장 철수하는 게 우선입니다.”
100|
101|“진정? 이 상황에 진정하게 생겼어요?”
102|
103|“마음을 가라앉히고 현실을 직시하라는 말씀을 드린 겁니다.”
104|
105|최 팀장의 침착한 목소리가 이어졌다.
106|
107|“다행히 늦지 않았습니다. 최대한 빨리 왔던 길을 돌아가면 한 시간 안에 밀림으로 진입할 수 있어요. 하지만 이런 황무지에서 놈과 맞닥트렸다가는…….”
108|
109|“그걸 누가 모르나? 간섭도 적당히 하세요.”
110|
111|웃음 많고 예의 바른 젠틀맨은 이제 없다. 원명훈의 신경질적인 모습에 최 팀장의 눈빛이 가라앉았다.
112|
113|“유감이네요. 그렇게 받아들이실 줄은 몰랐습니다.”
114|
115|“유감? 협동, 협동 하니까 진짜 동급으로 보이나 본데…… 시발, 말해 봤자 입만 아프지. 어쨌건 나한테 이래라저래라할 생각은 집어치워요. 안 그래도 기분 더러우니까.”
116|
117|위기에 처하면 그 사람의 본모습을 알 수 있다고 했다.
118|
119|그런 의미에서 원명훈이라는 사람은 딱 이 정도였다. 이런 사람을 우상으로 생각했다는 사실이 씁쓸할 뿐이다.
120|
121|원명훈이 초조한 얼굴로 길드원들에게 말했다.
122|
123|“마정석만 챙겨. 최대한 빨리 게이트 입구로 돌아간다.”
124|
125|게이트를 빠져나가는 문은 두 개다. 진입하는 입구와 보스 몬스터를 죽이면 열리는 출구.
126|
127|현재로서는 당연히 전자를 택하는 것이 옳은 선택이다.
128|
129|“넵.”
130|
131|준비는 신속하게 끝났다. 다만 여전히 창백하게 질려 있는 1팀장이 문제였다.
132|
133|“저 양반 왜 저래?”
134|
135|내 중얼거림에 시종일관 한 걸음 뒤에서 말을 아끼고 있던 김 집사가 대답했다.
136|
137|“몬스터의 피어(Fear)에 노출됐군요.”
138|
139|“A급 헌터가요?”
140|
141|“상대는 네임드 몬스터니까요.”
142|
143|“아.”
144|
145|“그리고 등급은 힘의 잣대일 뿐입니다. 정신력이 굳건한 것과는 아무런 상관이 없죠.”
146|
147|아무리 그렇다고 해도 A급 헌터가 피어에 걸리다니.
148|
149|둘 중 하나다. 1팀장이 평소에 심약한 정신력의 소유자거나, 네임드 몬스터가 그만큼 강한 놈이거나.
150|
151|‘개인적으로는 전자였으면 좋겠는데.’
152|
153|나는 그런 생각을 하며 1팀장을 향해 다가갔다. 몸이라도 일으켜 세워 주기 위해서였는데, 그는 뭔가에 데인 것처럼 화들짝 놀랐다.
154|
155|“괜찮아요. 해치려는 거 아닙니다. 저 알죠?”
156|
157|“지, 진태경.”
158|
159|“아직 멀쩡하시네. 그럼 이제 정신 차리고 일어납시다. 아니면 계속 앉아 계시다가 먹잇감 되시든지.”
160|
161|“으헉!”
162|
163|간혹 어떨 때는 용기보다 공포를 부추기는 것이 낫다.
164|
165|먹잇감이라는 말에 벌떡 일어난 1팀장이 불안한 눈으로 주위를 둘러봤다.
166|
167|“노, 놈은?”
168|
169|“여기 없어요. 그나저나 어떻게 살아온 겁니까?”
170|
171|아까부터 묻고 싶었던 말이다. 네임드 몬스터라는 단어가 튀어나온 순간부터 아무도 궁금해하지 않았지만.
172|
173|내 물음에 1팀장이 입술을 잘근잘근 씹었다.
174|
175|“선택의 여지가 없었어.”
176|
177|“……그랬군요.”
178|
179|도망쳤구나. 팀원들을 버리고.
180|
181|하지만 나는 비난하지 않았다. 그를 이해해서가 아니라, 나 자신에게 그럴 만한 자격이 없다고 생각했기 때문이다.
182|
183|‘욕을 할 수는 있겠지만 적어도 나는 아니야.’
184|
185|내 마음을 아는지 모르는지, 1팀장은 횡설수설 말을 늘어놓았다.
186|
187|“조심스럽게 접근하고 있었는데, 놈이 우릴 봤어. 그리고 날개를, 검은 날개를 활짝 펴고…….”
188|
189|“검은 날개?”
190|
191|“그, 그래. 머리부터 꼬리까지 온통 흑색이었어.”
192|
193|문득 떠오르는 기억이 있다. 동굴 안을 가득 메우던 비명과 거대한 날개를.
194|
195|그때 만났던 그 와이번도 몸 전체가 흑색이었다.
196|
197|“블랙 와이번.”
198|
199|“아니야, 달라. 지금까지 봤던 블랙 와이번보다 몇 배는 크고 강했어. 놈은…… 진짜 괴물이야.”
200|
201|그렇다면 3년 전 마주쳤던 그놈은 아닐 것이다.
202|
203|상동역 변이 게이트 사건 이후 나는 숱한 조사를 받았다. 사건 진상을 파견하기 위해 현장을 방문한 조사팀은 그놈이 일반적인 블랙 와이번의 범주에서 크게 벗어나지 못한다는 결론을 내렸다.
204|
205|‘그렇다면 그놈은 지금쯤 어디에 있을까.’
206|
207|게이트 안의 몬스터는 일정 시간마다 리젠 된다. 때문에 조사반이 도착했을 때, 놈은 이미 사라진 후였다.
208|
209|간혹 술을 마실 때마다 나는 그런 생각을 하고는 했다.
210|
211|그놈은 지금쯤 어디 있을까, 혹시 다른 헌터의 손에 죽은 것은 아닐까. 만약 살아 있다면 복수할 기회는 있을까.
212|
213|‘이제는 가능해.’
214|
215|양쪽 모두가 살아 있는 한, 언젠가 다시 만날 날이 올 것이다.
216|
217|나는 놈에게, 놈은 나에게. 서로가 서로에게 씻을 수 없는 기억을 안겨 주었으니까.
218|
219|하지만 오늘은 그 날이 아닌 모양이다.
220|
221|“진태경 씨.”
222|
223|“태경아!”
224|
225|어느새 준비를 끝마친 길드원들이 나를 기다리고 있었다. 그리고 대열에 합류하기 위해 걸음을 뗀 그 순간이었다.
226|
227|“외눈.”
228|
229|1팀장의 입에서 불현듯 튀어나온 한 단어에 몸이 덜컥 굳는다.
230|
231|천천히 돌아서자 떨리는 손으로 자신의 눈을 가리키는 1팀장이 보였다.
232|
233|“지금, 뭐라고.”
234|
235|“맞아. 한쪽 눈이 망가져 있었어. 꼭 뭔가에 찔린 것처럼…….”
236|
237|“……!”
238|
239|순간 전류가 등줄기를 타고 흘렀다. 머릿속이 새하얗게 물들고 주먹에 저절로 힘이 들어간다.
240|
241|3년 전, 나는 죽음을 각오하고 놈에게 달려들었다.
242|
243|모든 힘을 끌어모아 일섬, 아니 ‘힘껏 찌르기’를 날렸고 창날은 정확히 놈의 눈동자에 꽂혔다.
244|
245|그것이 내가 할 수 있는 마지막 발악이었고, 녀석에게 남긴 유일한 흔적이 되었다.
246|
247|‘놈이다.’
248|
249|평범한 블랙 와이번이 어떻게 네임드 몬스터가 되었는지에 대한 의문은 떠오르지 않았다.
250|
251|솜털까지 바짝 곤두선 피부가 증인이고 두방망이질 치는 심장이 검사인 동시에 판사다.
252|
253|나를 이루는 모든 것들이 입을 모아 외치고 있었다.
254|
255|1팀장이 말한 정체불명의 네임드 몬스터가, 3년 전 내게 씻을 수 없는 악몽을 안겨 준 바로 그놈이라고.
256|
257|‘드디어 만났다.’
258|
259|이 감정을 뭐라고 표현해야 할지 모르겠다.
260|
261|두려움? 기쁨?
262|
263|알 수 없는 감정으로 전신이 부르르 떨렸다.
264|
265|그 어느 때보다 팽팽하게 날 선 감각에 짙은 혈향(血香)이 섞여든 그때였다.
266|
267|- 캬우우우우우!
268|
269|멀리서 들려오는 포효에 나는 고개를 들었다.
270|
271|석양이 지고 있는 황무지의 지평선에서, 온통 흑빛으로 물든 날개가 이쪽으로 날아오고 있었다.
272|
273|
274|
275|* * *
276|
277|
278|
279|‘빌어먹을. 빌어먹을. 빌어먹을!’
280|
281|원명훈의 마음속에서는 끊임없이 욕설이 반복 재생 되고 있었다.
282|
283|이미 계획은 끝장난 거나 다름없었다. 이제는 목숨마저 걱정해야 할 판국이다.
284|
285|‘네임드 몬스터라니.’
286|
287|8년 전만큼, 아니 오히려 그때보다 더욱 심각한 상황이다.
288|
289|길드원들을 닦달해서 빠르게 준비를 끝마친 원명훈이 막 출발 지시를 내리려던 순간이었다.
290|
291|“옵니다.”
292|
293|귓가를 파고드는 나직한 목소리에 심장이 쿵 내려앉는다.
294|
295|그 목소리의 주인이 진태경이라서 더더욱 그랬다.
296|

“No, it was different. It was several times larger and stronger than any Black Wyvern I’d ever seen. That thing… it’s a real monster.”

[P99]
Then it couldn’t have been the same creature I’d encountered three years ago.

[P100]
After the Sangdong Station Mutated Gate incident, I had been subjected to countless investigations. The team dispatched to investigate the truth behind the incident had concluded that the creature didn’t fall far outside the normal range for a Black Wyvern.

[P101]
*Then where is it now?*

[P102]
Monsters inside Gates respawned at regular intervals. By the time the investigators arrived, it had already disappeared.

[P103]
Whenever I drank, I sometimes found myself wondering.

[P104]
*Where is it now? Did another Hunter kill it? If it’s still alive, will I ever get the chance to take revenge?*

[P105]
*I could do it now.*

[P106]
As long as we were both alive, the day would eventually come when we met again.

[P107]
I had left it with an indelible memory, and it had done the same to me.

[P108]
But apparently, that day wasn’t today.

[P109]
“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”

[P110]
“Taekyung!”

[P111]
The Guild members had finished preparing and were waiting for me. I had just started toward the formation when—

[P112]
“One eye.”

[P113]
The two words that suddenly fell from Team Leader 1’s lips brought me to a dead stop.

[P114]
I slowly turned around. Team Leader 1 pointed to one of his own eyes with a trembling hand.

[P115]
“What did you just say?”

[P116]
“That’s right. One of its eyes was ruined. Like something had stabbed it…”

[P117]
“…!”

[P118]
Electricity raced down my spine. My mind went blank, and my fists clenched of their own accord.

[P119]
Three years ago, I had charged at that creature prepared to die.

[P120]
I had gathered every last ounce of strength and unleashed One Annihilation—no, *Stab with All My Strength*. The spearhead had buried itself squarely in its eye.

[P121]
That had been my final act of defiance, and the only mark I’d managed to leave on it.

[P122]
*It’s that bastard.*

[P123]
I didn’t stop to wonder how an ordinary Black Wyvern had become a Named Monster.

[P124]
Every hair standing on end across my skin bore witness, and my pounding heart served as both prosecutor and judge.

[P125]
Everything that made me who I was cried out with one voice.

[P126]
The unidentified Named Monster Team Leader 1 had described was the very creature that had left me with an indelible nightmare three years ago.

[P127]
*We finally meet again.*

[P128]
I didn’t know what to call this feeling.

[P129]
Fear? Joy?

[P130]
My whole body trembled with an emotion I couldn’t name.

[P131]
My senses were drawn tighter and sharper than ever when the thick scent of blood drifted into them.

[P132]
—Kyaaaaaaaah!

[P133]
I raised my head at the roar echoing from the distance.

[P134]
On the horizon of the wasteland beneath the setting sun, a pair of pitch-black wings was flying toward us.

[P135]
* * *

[P136]
*Goddammit. Goddammit. Goddammit!*

[P137]
The curse repeated endlessly in Won Myunghoon’s mind.

[P138]
His plan was as good as ruined. Now he even had to worry about getting out alive.

[P139]
*A Named Monster.*

[P140]
This was as serious as the situation eight years ago—no, it was even worse.

[P141]
Won Myunghoon had hurried the Guild members through their preparations and was just about to order them to move out when—

[P142]
“It’s coming.”

[P143]
The low voice piercing his ears made his heart plummet.

[P144]
All the more so because it belonged to Jin Taekyung.

[P145]
“W-what do you mean?”

[P146]
“Prepare for battle. Or run for your life.”

[P147]
“I’m asking what the hell you mean!”

[P148]
“What else could I mean?”

[P149]
There was something unfamiliar about Jin Taekyung’s dark, steady gaze.

[P150]
The man before Won Myunghoon now was neither his rabid fan nor the foolish kid in his twenties who had grinned at him like an idiot.

[P151]
*What is this feeling?*

[P152]
Won Myunghoon flinched as Jin Taekyung spoke in a dry voice.

[P153]
“Take everyone with you. I still have the necklace.”

[P154]
“…What?”

[P155]
What the hell was this bastard talking about?

[P156]
As Won Myunghoon stared at him in confusion, one corner of Jin Taekyung’s mouth curled upward.

[P157]
“Why are you so surprised? Did you think I wouldn’t know?”

[P158]
“You—you bastard.”

[P159]
“Myunghoon hyung. No, Mr. Won Myunghoon.”

[P160]
Won Myunghoon froze. Not from humiliation, but from the crushing pressure bearing down on him.

[P161]
A pressure unlike anything he had felt from Jin Taekyung before was pouring off him.

[P162]
“Whatever you did or planned to do, I’ll let everything up to this point slide. But…”

[P163]
Beneath the tangled hair falling over his face, his darkened eyes gleamed.

[P164]
“Never bare your teeth at me again.”

[P165]
“…!”

[P166]
“I’m done. Get lost.”

[P167]
Won Myunghoon’s lips moved, but no words came out.

[P168]
He stared at Jin Taekyung with an unreadable look, then spun around.

[P169]
He could feel the Peace Guild members’ gazes boring into the back of his head. Only now had they realized something had been going on.

[P170]
*Fucking idiots. How dare they…*

[P171]
But it didn’t matter.

[P172]
Jin Taekyung and those ragtag Guild members would all be dead soon anyway.

[P173]
A short while later, as Won Myunghoon and the Star Guild members ran with all their might, they heard a roar echo from far behind them.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

[P124]

[P125]

[P126]

[P129]

[P130]

[P131]

[P149]

[P150]

[P151]

[P154]

[P155]

[P156]

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 219

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃219화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|인류는 대격변 초기부터 지금까지, 숱한 죽음과 파괴의 경험을 바탕으로 몬스터를 분류하고 서열을 정립해 왔다.
  6|
  7|그에 따라 서식하는 몬스터의 등급에 따라 해당 게이트의 등급도 정해졌다.
  8|
  9|그러나…….
 10|
 11|‘어디에나 예외는 있는 법.’
 12|
 13|변이 게이트가 바로 그랬다. 인간이 정한 테두리를 벗어난 그것은 말 그대로 변이(變異), 그 자체였다.
 14|
 15|인류에게 있어 여전히 불가사의로 취급받는 게이트라는 공간에, 또 다른 변수가 끼어든 것이다.
 16|
 17|‘최악이지.’
 18|
 19|F급 게이트에서 D급 몬스터가, D급 게이트에서 B급 몬스터가 나타날 수도 있다.
 20|
 21|그것만으로도 끔찍한 악몽인데 더 큰 문제가 하나 남아 있었다.
 22|
 23|‘레어 몬스터(Rare Monster).’
 24|
 25|생각지도 못한 상위 몬스터와 마주친 것도 지랄 같은데, 그렇게 출현한 놈들은 하나같이 동급의 몬스터를 뛰어넘는 힘을 지녔다.
 26|
 27|레어 몬스터라는 단어는 그때 처음 탄생했다.
 28|
 29|그리고 얼마 지나지 않아 한 가지 의견이 제기되었다.
 30|
 31|
 32|
 33|‘그럼 A급 변이 게이트에서 나타나는 레어 몬스터들은? 같은 급으로 치기에는 너무 강하지 않나?’
 34|
 35|
 36|
 37|헌터들에게 A급이란 한 번의 각성으로 도달할 수 있는 최고점의 영역.
 38|
 39|그중에서도 강자로 인정받은 자들에게는 랭커라는 영광스러운 칭호가 부여되었다.
 40|
 41|이는 몬스터에게도 적용되는 문제였다. 관련 학계의 수많은 갑론을박 끝에 새로운 명칭이 생겨났다.
 42|
 43|‘네임드 몬스터(Named Monster).’
 44|
 45|A급이라는 울타리를 벗어난 진정한 괴수들.
 46|
 47|홀로 살아 돌아온 1팀장은 바로 그 네임드 몬스터가 있다고 말했다.
 48|
 49|우리가 서 있는 바로 공간, 와이번의 둥지에.
 50|
 51|“개소리!”
 52|
 53|거칠게 소리친 원명훈이 1팀장의 멱살을 움켜잡았다.
 54|
 55|“네임드 몬스터라니, 그딴 게 여기 있을 리가 없어.”
 56|
 57|“저, 정말입니다. 제 눈으로 똑똑히 봤다고요.”
 58|
 59|1팀장이 떨리는 목소리로 말을 이었다.
 60|
 61|“평범한 와이번보다 몇 배는 거대했습니다. 두 눈으로 직접 보면서도 믿기지 않을 정도로.”
 62|

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
